sources.title: Evgeny Spodarev, Spatial Statistics: Lecture Notes (2024)
sources.locator: Complete focused unit, PDF pp. 3–8, Sections 1.1–1.2; inspected cached extracted-text lines 130–373. Includes field/stationarity/intrinsic definitions, covariance-kernel positivity, spectral representation, and Gaussian FDD conventions.

contents.name: PDF pp. 4–5: real random field, strict and wide stationarity, isotropy, and order-two intrinsic stationarity with displacement-dependent increment first and second moments
PDF p. 5, Proposition 1.6 and Exercise 1.7: covariance kernels are positive semidefinite, with the proof left as an exercise to expand a variance
contents.reason: The source states the characterization and gives the variance route but leaves it as an exercise; the local lemma supplies the complete finite-variance argument.

contents.name: PDF pp. 5–6: Bochner representation of a continuous positive-semidefinite stationary covariance by a finite spectral measure
contents.reason: The notes refer to the 2009 draft for Bochner; the local proof uses the published LCA Bochner supplier and explicitly carries AC and DC.

contents.name: PDF p. 7: Gaussian field defined by Gaussian finite-dimensional laws and determined by its mean and covariance
contents.reason: The notes do not verify consistency of singular Gaussian marginals or the extension hypotheses; the local proof does both and limits the conclusion to the cylinder sigma-algebra.

contents.name: PDF p. 8: the H=1 one-dimensional random-line case and its quadratic variogram

sources.title: Evgeny Spodarev, Random Fields I: Lecture Notes (Draft, 2009)
sources.locator: Complete focused units, PDF pp. 14–20 and 35–46; inspected cached extracted-text lines 815–1229 and 1820–2990. Includes §§1.3–1.4, Theorem 2.1.1, and Proposition 2.2.1.

contents.name: PDF pp. 16–20, §§1.3–1.4: field moments/covariance, strict and wide stationarity, isotropy, and stationary increments
PDF p. 19, Definition 1.4.3: the draft's order-two intrinsic stationarity also requires zero mean increments
contents.reason: The controlling design follows the broader 2024 wide-increment convention, allowing the increment mean to depend on displacement; the zero-mean restriction is not imported.

contents.name: PDF p. 35, Theorem 2.1.1: Bochner–Khinchin representation, with the displayed proof in dimension one and the general-dimensional proof referred to an external source
contents.reason: The local proof invokes the library's proved general LCA theorem, so no unproved general-dimensional argument is imported from this draft.

contents.name: PDF pp. 43–44, Proposition 2.2.1(4): conditional negative definiteness from a variance of finite increments
contents.reason: The draft prints complex weights without conjugation; this item uses the controlling plan's real coefficients and gives a complete local expansion.

contents.name: PDF p. 45, Example 2.2.1(1): a random linear function has a quadratic intrinsic variogram
PDF p. 43, Proposition 2.2.1(6): the Schoenberg converse is cited rather than proved
contents.reason: The controlling design expressly omits the converse; the valid quadratic variogram is witnessed by an explicit field instead.

sources.title: Hermine Biermé, Introduction to random fields and scale invariance: Lecture I (2016)
sources.locator: Complete 29-page lecture PDF; inspected the full relevant units on PDF pp. 4–6 and 12–19, covering random fields, covariance positivity, stationarity, Bochner representation, and stationary increments.

contents.name: PDF pp. 4–6: coordinate random fields, finite-dimensional laws, second-order fields, covariance positive-definiteness, and Gaussian FDDs
contents.reason: The independent lecture states the covariance criterion; the local lemma proves the variance argument in full.

contents.name: PDF pp. 12–13: stationary covariance functions are positive type and have a Bochner spectral measure
contents.reason: The lecture states the theorem without its proof; the local item supplies the proof through the library Bochner result.

contents.name: PDF pp. 18–19: stationary increments, variograms, and the zero-sum negative-type inequality
contents.reason: The lecture states the inequality; the local item proves it for the plan's real coefficients and moment-only order-two hypothesis.
